title: [finding] service-analytics: every default boot logs a WARN that no "security" service was registered at init, although the Security plugin registers moments later — the sibling `getReadScope` path logs the same situation at `info`
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect with a named landing spot and a reproduction (`finding` class (a): a false-alarm WARN reproduced on every boot of the default composition; also the shape AGENTS.md "Startup registry reads" names as a defect).
reach: public entry measured once — `npx os dev --ui` / `npx os start --artifact` on a fresh `npm create objectstack@latest` project prints the WARN under "Boot diagnostics" on three consecutive boots while `Plugins: 41 loaded … Security …` is on the same banner.
Reader: `domain:services` seat (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts`, the `admitObjectRead` branch around lines 1446–1455).
Dedup: `search_issues` "Analytics No admitObjectRead configured and no security service registered at init warning on every boot" (open + closed) → 0 cards on the warning itself; #3618 (closed) introduced the per-query bridge this warning describes and is the prior ruling to read.
Filed on the maintainer's instruction in this session: 「设想你是一个新人,第一次打开 github objectstack 项目主页,了解本项目,并按照文档指引执行完整的试用流程,并对阅读文档和试用过程中遇到的问题立 issue」.

## Summary

A freshly scaffolded project (`npm create objectstack@latest`, blank template, default plugin set — 41 plugins loaded, `Security` among them) prints this in **Boot diagnostics** on every `os dev` / `os start`:

```text
WARN [Analytics] No admitObjectRead configured and no "security" service registered at init — the bridge resolves per query,
but if no security service ever appears, analytics queries will NOT enforce the OBJECT-LEVEL read grant. On a SQL driver
that means any authenticated caller can post an inline dataset and read counts and groupings for an object they hold no
grant on. Supply admitObjectRead or register a security service.
```

The security service does appear on the same boot. `packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` (around line 1420–1455) handles the two bridges differently for the identical condition "security not registered yet at my `init`, bridge resolves per query":

- `getReadScope` bridge → `ctx.logger.info('[Analytics] getReadScope bridged to the "security" service; that service is not registered yet at init and will be resolved per query (plugin order is not significant).')`
- `admitObjectRead` bridge → `ctx.logger.warn(…)` with the text above, warning about a consequence that only holds if no security service **ever** registers.

So on the default composition the WARN is a false alarm, repeated on every boot, and it is the first security-sounding line a newcomer reads in their new project. It is also the shape AGENTS.md's "Startup registry reads — never record a verdict the boot can still contradict" rule describes: a read of the service registry during `init()`, a terminal conclusion drawn from "absent", recorded as a `warn` that nothing later retracts when the provider registers.

## Reproduction

`@objectstack/cli@17.7.0`, `@objectstack/service-analytics@17.7.0`, Node v22.22.0.

```bash
npm create objectstack@latest my-app && cd my-app
npx os dev --ui          # or: npx os start --artifact ./dist/objectstack.json after `pnpm run build`
```

Boot output: `Plugins: 41 loaded … Security … AnalyticsServicePlugin …` followed by `⚠ Boot diagnostics — 4 warnings logged during startup`, one of which is the line quoted above. Reproduced on three consecutive boots (existing SQLite DB and `--fresh`).

## Expected

Per-query resolution is the designed behaviour, so init-time absence of `security` is not a problem to warn about. Either log it at `info` like the `getReadScope` sibling, or defer the verdict to `kernel:ready` / `kernel:bootstrapped` and warn only if the security service is still absent then (cure 1 and cure 3 in the AGENTS.md rule).

## Actual

A `warn` fires on every default boot describing a data-exposure consequence that does not apply to the running composition.
